_comment: CAN THE OBJECT BASELINE BE RE-DERIVED? MEASURED, AND THE ANSWER IS IN TWO PARTS.
`published-object-set.json` beside this file records 138,287 objects with whole-tree and
per-class digests, taken on 2026-09-15 off the tree the genesis-to-tip publish of
2026-09-10 left on disk. It says of itself that the tree is machine-local, `.gitignore`d,
and will not survive the machine. IT HAS NOT. Searched on 2026-09-18 across the build
area and the whole home tree to six directory levels for a `.chain-state` directory or
for that reading's own generation id: no match. So its digests can no longer be
recomputed here, and a comparison against them is a comparison against a record rather
than against a tree.
THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE BASELINE BEING UNCHECKABLE, AND THIS FILE IS THE PART THAT
IS. Two contiguous ranges of the same chain were fetched, ingested and published fresh on
2026-09-18 and measured with the same tool. What they establish is not the count — 2,200
blocks are not 75,971 — but the two things a count cannot carry on its own:
1. THE IDENTITY THAT GENERATES THE COUNT HOLDS, at two scales, exactly. A published
metadata-only tree is `blocks + 3 x transactions + 6` objects: 200 + 3 x 23 + 6 =
275, and 2,200 + 3 x 367 + 6 = 3,307, both observed rather than predicted. The same
identity gives the recorded 75,971 + 3 x 20,770 + 6 = 138,287, and the ten object
classes are the same ten, with the same shapes, in both readings.
2. THE NOISE FLOOR OF A BYTE-FOR-BYTE COMPARISON, which is what anyone comparing two
published trees has to know before calling a difference a regression. The 200-block
range was fetched TWICE, eight minutes apart, from the live chain, and ingested at a
pinned generation both times. Object count, byte total and `pathDigest` are
IDENTICAL: the key set is fully reproducible from the chain. Nine of the ten classes
are byte-identical too. The tenth is ONE object — the generation's `summary.json` —
and the whole difference is three fields that describe the RUN and not the chain:
`capturedAt`, `tipAtCapture` and `replayableWindowBlocks`. So a re-run that differs
in one object, in those fields, has not regressed; a re-run that moves `pathDigest`
has.
THE INGEST ITSELF IS DETERMINISTIC AND THE FETCH IS NOT, WHICH IS WHERE THAT ONE OBJECT
COMES FROM. Re-ingesting one snapshot at one generation reproduces all four figures
exactly, digests included. The per-row `observedAt` a fetch stamps reaches NO published
object (measured: zero files in the tree contain it), so the only wall-clock that
survives into the tree is the one in `summary.json`.
AND THE WHOLE-CHAIN READING COULD NOT SIMPLY BE RE-TAKEN, FOR A REASON WORTH RECORDING.
See `producerGap` below: the range producer does not write the facts the reader now
requires of every row, so the path that published the 138,287-object tree cannot publish
a tree this reader accepts without a migration step in the middle. That is a defect in
the producer and not in the baseline, but it is the reason this file measures ranges
rather than the chain.

_comment: THE RANGE PRODUCER CANNOT WRITE A SNAPSHOT THIS READER ACCEPTS, AND IT IS FOUR MEMBERS.
The facts lifted out of the reader and into snapshot data are supplied by
`tools/chain/lib/producer-facts.mjs`. Three producers import it — `backfill-blocks.mjs`,
`capture-chain.mjs` and `follow-chain.mjs`. `ingest-range.mjs` does not, and it is the
one a range-by-range backfill runs. Its row construction writes `transactionFee` and
stops there.
Reproduced on a freshly fetched range, rc 1 and zero objects written:
[S5-ROW-MEMBERS-REQUIRED] a transaction row ... carries no `cost`
Running `tools/chain/migrate-chain-facts.mjs --write` over the merged snapshot supplies
all four and the same ingest then exits 0 — so the gap is exactly these members and
nothing else is wrong with the path. The repair is the import the three siblings already
have; the migration in the middle is a workaround and is not one a backfill should need.
MEASURED HERE BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHETHER A FORMAT-TOKEN BUMP CAN COEXIST WITH A
BYTE-FOR-BYTE COMPARISON. A producer built from this tree, handed a snapshot carrying an
unreadable token, does not write a partial tree — it writes NOTHING. So a comparison
between a producer that knows a newer token and one that does not is not a diff with a
few named lines in it; one side is absent, which is the same signature a broken
comparison has.
